tree.capped: Only the first {{shown}} of {{count}} steps are shown.
tree.offloaded: The controller keeps this workflow's steps in its database (offloaded node status): they are not in the object, so they cannot be shown here.
tree.compressed: The controller stored this workflow's steps compressed: they cannot be shown here.

dialog.suspendText: The workflow starts no new steps until it is resumed; steps already running go on, as argo suspend does.
dialog.resumeText: The workflow's suspension is lifted and every suspend step that is waiting is marked Succeeded, as argo resume does.
dialog.stopText: Running steps are stopped and no new ones start, but exit handlers still run, as argo stop does.
dialog.terminateText: Running steps are stopped and nothing else runs, exit handlers included, as argo terminate does.
dialog.patch: Sent to the workflow (a JSON merge patch):
dialog.versioned: The resourceVersion shown is the one read when this dialog opened; it is read again right before sending and the fresh one is sent, so the API server refuses the change if the workflow changes in between; nothing is retried.
dialog.stamped: The finishedAt shown is set anew to the time of sending.
dialog.changed: The workflow changed while this dialog was open. Check the updated change and confirm again.

nothing.suspend: Nothing to change: the workflow is already suspended.
nothing.resume: Nothing to change: the workflow is not suspended and no suspend step is waiting.
nothing.stop: Nothing to change: the workflow is already being stopped.
nothing.terminate: Nothing to change: the workflow is already being terminated.

refusal.completed: A completed workflow cannot be suspended.
refusal.finished: The workflow has already finished, so there is nothing to stop.
refusal.nodesElsewhere: The workflow's nodes are compressed or kept in the controller's database, so Sextant cannot resume its suspend steps. Run argo resume {{name}} -n {{namespace}} instead.
refusal.noDefault: The suspend step {{step}} waits for its output parameter {{parameter}}, which has no value and no default, so it cannot be resumed. Set it with argo node set first.

retryHint: Sextant does not retry workflows: a retry resets the failed nodes and deletes their pods, which the Argo server does. Run argo retry {{name}} -n {{namespace}}.
